implementation_notes: Python's idiom is one frozen dataclass per legal shape, unioned in a type alias, with Enum or Literal tags where a single class carries the state and a validating classmethod (__post_init__ or try_parse) as the only door - the classic sealed hierarchy is replaced by this union of value types checked by mypy or pyright. Exhaustiveness is not enforced by the runtime: the final branch of an if/elif chain or match statement must call typing.assert_never(state) (or the project must enable mypy --enable-error-code exhaustive-match / pyright reportMatchNotExhaustive), which turns a forgotten variant into a checker error. Because annotations are not enforced at run time, keep validation in the factory and validate untrusted input there rather than trusting the annotation.
pitfalls: Annotations are not enforced at run time: a dataclass accepts any value for a field unless __post_init__ or the factory validates it, so the 'proof' exists only for callers the checker sees.
A forgotten final assert_never(state) compiles and passes: without the assert (or the exhaustive-match diagnostic) the checker reports nothing and the missing variant returns None silently.
frozen=True blocks attribute assignment only - a mutable field (list, dict) still lets callers change the state after construction, and object.__setattr__ bypasses the freeze entirely.

variants.name: Structural pattern matching over the variants
variants.idiom_name: match statement with class patterns + assert_never in the wildcard arm
variants.implementation_notes: Python 3.10 adds structural pattern matching (PEP 634): the same union of dataclasses is consumed by match with class patterns, which destructures the variant's fields in the case header. mypy and pyright can check a match for exhaustiveness directly (mypy --enable-error-code exhaustive-match, pyright reportMatchNotExhaustive), so the wildcard arm can hold assert_never(unreachable) - or be dropped when the diagnostic is enabled. Prefer this variant on 3.10 and later: it removes the isinstance chain and makes the per-variant payload visible in the branch, while the type checker still proves that every legal shape is handled.
variants.code_sketch:
def describe(state: ConnectionState) -> str:
    match state:
        case Disconnected():
            return "down"
        case Connected(session_id=session_id):
            return session_id
        case _ as unreachable:
            assert_never(unreachable)   # mypy/pyright: exhaustive match
pitfalls: A bare ignore-case (case _: pass) or a missing assert_never silences the check; the exhaustive-match diagnostic must actually be enabled in the project configuration.

Class patterns match by isinstance - a subclass of a variant matches its case too, so hierarchy misuse can still route a value into the wrong branch unless the variants are final by convention (no subclassing).
match binds names by assignment, and a capture pattern (case session_id) matches anything, shadowing the intended variant - always use the class pattern form or dotted names for values.
